title: Concept Algebra for (Score-Based) Text-Controlled Generative Models
role: Theory of when a concept is a subspace of the score, and the score-difference projection that edits it
reads: The diffusion model's noise prediction at the current noisy sample, for the original, new, empty and subspace-spanning prompts
trained_on: nothing trained for the method; one deliberately overfitted DreamBooth fine-tune for the toy example
score_enters: Each step replaces the prompt's score on the concept subspace with the new prompt's score, then applies classifier-free guidance
adding_scores: Scores add over two concepts if the image is causally separable with respect to them; a score difference isolates a concept only if the prompts share the other concept's distribution
properties: Prompt match partly (human ranking of style and content); counting, binding, spatial relation, position and size not tested
unseen: no: rare content and style pairs are used, with no held-out concepts
headline: In a human ranking of faithfulness to style and content, the average proportion (0 to 1, higher is better) is 0.476 for concept algebra against 0.164 for concept composition and 0.162 for direct prompting, over 49 content and style pairs and 10 raters on Stable Diffusion
copy_or_avoid: Copy the rule that a sentence pair must differ only on the target property; avoid assuming binding or left-right order is causally separable (inferred)
